title: High-dimensional ridge return forecast with chronological penalty selection
prompt:
Select the ridge penalty for a high-dimensional return-forecasting regression by chronological validation, refit on the pooled training and validation rows with correct rescaling, and contrast the honest test error with the error that an illicit test-set selection would report.

Data (synthetic panel): each element of `rows` is {t: integer period, x: [P signals in feature_names order, observed at the end of period t], y: target return for period t+1 (decimal), already aligned to x so no further lag is needed}. Rows are NOT sorted: sort ascending by t. Walking forward in t, the first split.train rows form the training set, the next split.validation rows the validation set and the final split.test rows the test set (the three blocks partition all rows). P exceeds the number of training rows, so unpenalized least squares has no unique solution.

Protocol:
1. Selection stage (every statistic from training rows only): mu_j and s_j = mean and ddof=1 standard deviation of feature j over the training rows; Z = (X - mu) / s; ybar = training mean of y. Ridge estimate for penalty lambda: beta(lambda) = (Z'Z + lambda I)^-1 Z'(y - ybar), with lambda added to Z'Z directly (no 1/n scaling) and no penalty on the intercept (handled by centering). Validation prediction for a row: ybar + ((x - mu)/s)' beta(lambda) using the TRAINING mu, s and ybar. validation_mse_by_lambda = mean squared error over validation rows, one entry per lambda in lambda_grid order.
2. lambda* = the grid value with the smallest validation MSE; exact ties go to the largest lambda.
3. Refit stage: pool training + validation rows, recompute mu, s and ybar from the pooled rows, and for EVERY lambda in the grid fit beta(lambda) on the pooled standardized data. Convert to raw-feature scale: b_j = beta_j / s_j and intercept a = ybar - sum_j b_j mu_j, so that prediction = a + x' b on unstandardized x. test_mse_by_lambda = test-row MSE of each pooled refit in grid order; test_mse_selected = the entry at lambda*; final_coefficients = [a, b_1, ..., b_P] at lambda* (intercept first, then feature_names order).
4. Illicit comparison: illicit_lambda = the grid value minimizing test_mse_by_lambda (ties to the largest lambda). It is reported only to quantify the optimism of choosing on the test set; the selected model remains lambda* and test_mse_selected must come from lambda*, not from illicit_lambda.

conventions.standardization: per-feature mean and ddof=1 standard deviation of the FIT sample only (training rows in the selection stage, pooled training+validation rows in the refit stage)
conventions.intercept: unpenalized; handled by centering y on the fit-sample mean
conventions.penalty: lambda added to Z^T Z directly, no 1/n scaling

outputs.name: validation_mse_by_lambda
outputs.description: Validation-row MSE of the training-only ridge fits, in lambda_grid order.

outputs.name: selected_lambda
outputs.description: lambda* minimizing validation MSE (largest lambda on exact ties).

outputs.name: final_coefficients
outputs.description: Pooled-refit model at lambda* on the raw feature scale: [intercept, b_1..b_P] in feature_names order.

outputs.name: test_mse_by_lambda
outputs.description: Test-row MSE of each pooled refit, in lambda_grid order.

outputs.name: test_mse_selected
outputs.description: Test-row MSE of the pooled refit at lambda* (the honest held-out estimate).

outputs.name: illicit_lambda
outputs.description: Grid value that would be chosen by minimizing test MSE (reported for contrast only).

instructions: Submit strict JSON with exactly one key, code, whose value is Python source defining solve(data). The controller supplies the inputs object as data. Return a JSON-native dictionary mapping every declared output name to its answer. Use Python stdlib and NumPy only; do not read files, access the network, spawn processes, or use native tools. Write a general calculation from data, not constants for this instance. Your program will also be evaluated on undisclosed changed inputs under the same conventions. The controller will execute the first submission and give you its public outputs or error once, then ask for a final code submission. It never reveals reference answers or hidden test results. Supporting numerical ledgers and diagnostics are the declared array outputs; follow their ordering exactly. No markdown fences around your JSON.

provenance.synthetic_inputs: Features and targets are generated from two latent factors, heterogeneous feature scales and offsets, eight of 52 nonzero true slopes, and Gaussian noise. These are stipulated evaluation inputs, not market observations.
provenance.protocol: Split sizes, grid and conventions are author-stipulated; the illicit comparison is a diagnostic, not a modelling choice.
provenance.vintage_limit: Not market data; no calendar or point-in-time interpretation applies.
